description: Run keys Orchestra and Unify must both produce byte-identically. The key is the create-or-adopt idempotency token: when the two sides disagree, the dispatcher cannot adopt the occurrence Orchestra projected and mints a second execution for the same slot. Two rows read as concurrency, and an overlap guard then skips every tick — the campaign runtime halted this way with no error anywhere.

cases.name: team destination and an offset timestamp are both normalized
a Z-suffixed timestamp normalizes to the same fragment
no destination omits the segment entirely
a triggered wake tails on the medium the projected row carries
a triggered medium is normalized like any other free-form fragment
a triggered wake with no medium falls through to the shared once

trigger_lane_notes: A dispatcher waking on a projected trigger row without remembered event provenance rebuilds the key from that row alone — its revision, destination and trigger medium — so those three cases are the adoption path. A firing that does carry a contact and message is a distinct occurrence with its own tail and is meant to mint its own row. Provider-event armed rows are not in this contract: Unify keys real provider-event runs with build_provider_event_run_key, which carries a binding segment and the full event identity digest, so nothing on that lane ever adopts the projected row.
